title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is treating transverse vibrations of an elastic lamina (Euler–Bernoulli beam) of length a, supported by pins ('styli') at both ends A and B, i.e. the simply supported (pinned–pinned) case. The trial mode is y = cos(θ²t)·Y(x), with Y = A cos Φ + B sin Φ + C e^Φ + D e^{-Φ} and Φ = θx/b. The inertial ('elementary') force per unit length is p = −Kc²(θ⁴/b⁴)y, where Kc² is the bending stiffness. The previous page used the conditions Y(0)=0 and Y''(0)=0 to get A=0 and C+D=0. It also found the pin reaction at A, E = −Kc²(θ³/b³)cos θ²t (−B+C−D), together with ∫₀ˣ p dx.

On this page, integrating once more from 0 gives the moment about the running point Y of the elementary forces on AY:
∫dx∫p dx = −Kc²(θ²/b²)cos θ²t (−A cos Φ − B sin Φ + C e^Φ + D e^{-Φ}) + Kc²(θ²/b²)cos θ²t (−A+C+D) + Kc²(θ³/b³)cos θ²t (−B+C−D)x.
I checked this by differentiation and it is correct.

Adding the moment of the pin force, Ex, cancels the linear term. Since −A+C+D=0, the constant term also vanishes. The total moment is then −Kc²(θ²/b²)cos θ²t (−A cos Φ − …), which is exactly minus the elastic moment Kc²y''. This is a consistency check of the force/moment formulation against the beam equation.

Euler then moves Y to the end B (Φ = ζ = θa/b). He requires equilibrium of all forces with the pin reaction F at B, and requires zero moment at B (no curvature at a pinned end): −A cos ζ − B sin ζ + C e^ζ + D e^{-ζ} = 0. On the next page this is combined with Y(a)=0, giving B sin ζ = 0 and C=D=0. Hence ζ = iπ, θ = iπb/a, the period is a²/(i²b²π), and the frequencies scale as i². These are the classical simply supported beam modes sin(iπx/a).
errors: Euler calls the expression −Kc²(θ²/b²)cos θ²t(−A cos ζ − B sin ζ + C e^ζ + D e^{-ζ}) the 'sum of all elementary forces together with the pin force E'. It is actually the total moment at B; it carries θ²/b² instead of θ³/b³, so it is dimensionally a moment.

The correct force sum at x=a is −Kc²(θ³/b³)cos θ²t (A sin ζ − B cos ζ + C e^ζ − D e^{-ζ}), so the reaction should be F = +Kc²(θ³/b³)cos θ²t (A sin ζ − B cos ζ + C e^ζ − D e^{-ζ}). For the eventual solution (A=C=D=0, ζ=iπ) this gives F = −Kc²(θ³/b³)B cos(iπ)cos θ²t ≠ 0. Euler's formula instead gives F = 0, so his stated pin reaction at B is wrong.
The slip does not affect the frequency equation. The two conditions actually used on the next page (zero moment at B and Y(a)=0) are correct, so the eigenvalues ζ = iπ are right.

ideas.what: Computing the bending moment at a section as the double integral of the inertial loading plus the moment of the end reaction, and checking that it equals minus the elastic moment Kc²y''.
ideas.modern_name: Shear-force/bending-moment integration for the Euler–Bernoulli beam (M'' = load)
ideas.where_published: E443 itself; also E40/E65 (Additamentum de curvis elasticis) for the lamina vibration theory

ideas.what: Pinned-end boundary conditions y=0, y''=0 at both ends, and determination of the end reactions.
ideas.where_published: E443 (Novi Comm. Petrop. 17); discussed by Truesdell in Opera omnia II.11/2

ideas.what: Leading to frequencies proportional to i² for the simply supported lamina.
ideas.modern_name: Eigenfrequencies of the simply supported beam, ω_i ∝ (iπ/a)²

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine step in Euler's well-known E443 derivation of simply supported beam modes, which Truesdell has documented. The only notable item is a small, unremarked slip in the formula for the pin reaction F, which does not affect the results.
transcription_corrections: No substantive corrections; the transcription matches the image. The θθ/bb and θ³/b³ factors and the signs in the three-line formula for ∫dx∫p dx are correctly read.
